title: Weekly Challenge: Live Industry Office Hours
hook: Students drop into a mentor's 30-minute office hours. Design the system that runs it live.
description: This week's challenge: design the backend for live industry office hours. A mentor opens a 30-minute slot; any number of students can join, raise a hand, ask questions in a shared queue, and watch answers in real time. When the slot ends, a recap of questions and answers is saved to the mentor's and students' records. Respect everyone's time: joining should take seconds, and a student who arrives late should instantly see the current state.
constraints: Up to 500 students may join a single session; about 50 sessions can run across the platform.
Question queue and answers must update in near real time, under two seconds.
A late joiner must load the current queue and answered questions on connect.
Recaps persist after a session ends; sessions are ephemeral but recaps are durable.

title: Peer Demo Feedback in Under a Minute
hook: A student posts a two-minute demo. Peers leave quick, structured feedback. Design the pipeline.
description: Design a system where students post short project demos, a video link plus a blurb, and peers leave structured feedback in under a minute: a few tags and one sentence. The feature must solve the empty room: a brand-new demo should still surface to a few relevant peers so it does not sit with zero responses. Feedback becomes part of the author's visible record.
constraints: Submitting feedback should take a peer under 60 seconds.
A new demo must be routed to at least a few potential reviewers automatically.
Feedback is public and attributed; it aggregates onto the author's profile.
Spam or low-effort feedback should be cheap to filter later, so keep the feedback shape structured.

title: Form a Cross-Major Build Team
hook: Students have different skills, schedules, and project interests. Help a new idea find four compatible teammates.
description: Design the service behind a team-formation board for four-to-six-week industry projects. A student posts a project idea, the roles or skills still needed, available hours, and a short working-style preference. The platform suggests a small, explainable set of potential teammates across majors. Each student can accept, decline, or save a match without exposing private contact information until both sides opt in.
constraints: A student should see useful suggestions within a few seconds of posting or updating an idea.
The same popular students must not be notified by every project at once.
Suggestions must explain why the match is relevant using only the profile fields the student chose to share.
The system must handle a burst of several thousand students browsing ideas during a campus event.

title: Six-Week Project Sprint Check-In
hook: A student team needs one lightweight rhythm for updates, blockers, and mentor visibility without adding meeting overhead.
description: Design a weekly check-in system for a student team working with an industry mentor. Each member can post what shipped, what they learned, and any blocker. The mentor gets one concise digest and can spend a few minutes responding where it matters. Teams should see their momentum across the six-week project, while future students can learn from the public retrospective after the team chooses what to share.
constraints: Each student check-in should take under three minutes to submit.
Mentors receive at most one digest per team each week unless a serious blocker is marked.
A digest must still send if one teammate forgets to check in by the cutoff.
Public retrospectives must exclude private drafts and team-only notes.

title: Mentor Feedback Inbox
hook: Industry mentors have ten minutes. Route the few feedback requests where their experience has the most value.
description: Design an asynchronous feedback inbox for industry mentors. Students can request input on a design decision, attach a short context card, and pick a category such as data, frontend, manufacturing, or product. The system batches low-urgency requests into a small digest, surfaces high-fit requests first, and gives students a clear status without promising an immediate answer. A mentor's public feedback becomes a trustworthy part of the student's learning record.
constraints: A mentor who gives ten minutes should see no more than five focused requests.
Students need an immediate acknowledgement and a clear status as their request moves through the queue.
Requests should expire gracefully instead of lingering forever without an answer.
The same request cannot be sent repeatedly to the same mentor after a refresh or retry.

title: Community Learning Library
hook: A team solves a problem once. Make its useful notes, diagrams, and lessons easy for the next team to find.
description: Design a searchable library of public project artifacts: architecture diagrams, retrospectives, useful links, and short notes about what a team learned. Students should be able to search by topic, skill, or industry area and discover related artifacts before starting a new challenge. The system must keep drafts private until an author publishes, track which source a user found helpful, and avoid making a single popular resource slow for everyone.
constraints: Search should return a useful first page in under one second for common topics.
Authors can publish a revision without breaking links shared by other students.
Drafts and private team notes must never appear in public search results.
A popular artifact may receive thousands of reads during a workshop.

title: Campus Challenge Registration Rush
hook: A one-day industry challenge has limited seats. Students should get a fair, clear answer when registration opens at noon.
description: Design registration for a short, mentor-led campus challenge with 200 seats. At noon, thousands of students may click Join at the same moment. The platform must reserve seats fairly, show a waitlist position, release abandoned reservations, and send participants a reminder before the event. The goal is a small first step into the community, not a recruiting funnel.
constraints: At least 5,000 registration attempts may arrive in the first minute.
No more than 200 confirmed seats can be issued, even with retries or double-clicks.
A student must receive a clear confirmation or waitlist result within a few seconds.
Unclaimed reservations expire after 15 minutes and offer the seat to the next waitlisted student.
